documents.unit: Office of the President (AI at CMU, AI Advisory Board)
documents.title: AI at CMU: Policy and Guidance
documents.stance_why: The document sets no ban or permission on student AI use itself. It states principles and data rules, and says "Provide clear guidance on acceptable use including syllabus statements and assignment directions", which leaves the decision to instructors, so delegates.
documents.summary: University page of draft principles, campus expectations on approved tools and regulated data, and links to data policies 3-30, 3-31, 3-42. It sets no classroom rule on AI and asks that syllabus statements and assignment directions carry the guidance.

units.why: The opening sentence says "Draft policy principles emphasize academic integrity, data privacy and security"; it states the scope and principles of the institution-wide framework, so P56 and informs, general phase, addressed to all.
units.anchor: Draft policy principles emphasize academic integrity, data privacy and security
units.frag_start: CMU’s use of AI is grounded

units.why: "AI should enhance learning and prepare graduates for an AI-rich workplace" gives the learning-and-career rationale, so P44 (professional skill), informs, general.
units.anchor: AI should enhance learning and prepare graduates for an AI-rich workplace

units.why: "Provide equitable access to AI education and tools, with clear expectations for use" is an equity principle directed at the institution, so P51 with admin as actor; it also mentions clear expectations but access is the main point.
units.anchor: Provide equitable access to AI education and tools, with clear expectations for use

units.why: "Institutional data stewardship and regulatory compliance are nonnegotiable" is a principle that sets data protection as fixed, so P50 and informs.
units.anchor: Institutional data stewardship and regulatory compliance are nonnegotiable

units.why: "Be explicit about when and how AI is used; model proper attribution" asks for disclosure and attribution of AI use, so P24 with should.
units.anchor: Be explicit about when and how AI is used; model proper attribution

units.why: "Support with governance, staffing, and evaluation to ensure continuous improvement" commits to ongoing review, so P54 (revisit regularly) and informs; no learning-evidence claim is made so P55 does not fit.
units.anchor: Support with governance, staffing, and evaluation to ensure continuous improvement

units.why: "Use institutionally approved tools when working with university data" tells users to prefer vetted tools for data, so P50; modality should from the imperative without a hard ban, and it is addressed to all.
units.anchor: Use institutionally approved tools when working with university data

units.why: "Do not input regulated data (e.g., HIPAA, CUI, PCI) into generative AI tools" is a prohibition on entering data, so P50 (protect personal data) and must-not.
units.anchor: Do not input regulated data (e.g., HIPAA, CUI, PCI) into generative AI tools

units.why: "Follow all applicable laws/policies (e.g., accessibility, copyright, research integrity, data security)" is a general compliance rule; no type is specific to it, so P56 (framework principle) and must.
units.anchor: Follow all applicable laws/policies

units.why: "Provide clear guidance on acceptable use including syllabus statements and assignment directions" requires syllabus and assignment-level AI statements, so P09, course-start; the actor is not named, so instructors are assumed.
units.anchor: Provide clear guidance on acceptable use including syllabus statements and assignment directions

units.why: "Community members are expected to follow these policies whenever using AI tools in teaching, learning, research, or administrative work" binds everyone to the listed policies, so P56 and must for all.
units.anchor: Community members are expected to follow these policies whenever using AI tools

units.why: Describing Policy 3-30, the page says it "prohibits entering institutional data into generative AI systems without proper prior written approval"; a data ban with an approval exception, so P50 and must-not.
units.anchor: prohibits entering institutional data into generative AI systems without proper prior written approval

units.why: On Policy 3-31: "Users may not upload CMU data to generative AI systems without prior written approval". Separate policy, same data-protection type P50, must-not.
units.anchor: Users may not upload CMU data to generative AI systems without prior written approval

units.why: Policy 3-42 "reinforces requirements for protecting institutional data when using AI technologies"; this describes a data-protection duty, P50, informs.
units.anchor: reinforces requirements for protecting institutional data when using AI technologies

units.why: "CMU continues to evaluate policies and practices" and reviews research integrity, IP and copyright areas; a statement that policy will be revisited, so P54 and informs, over-time.
units.anchor: CMU continues to evaluate policies and practices to address emerging AI-related opportunities and risks

documents.unit: Office of Curriculum and Instructional Support
documents.title: Planning for AI in Teaching and Learning
documents.stance_why: The page says "There is no single approach to AI that will work for every course" and offers three approaches (limited, guided, integrated) for instructors to choose, so it delegates and lists tiers.
documents.summary: Faculty planning guide that offers three approaches (limited, guided, integrated), five questions for deciding, and advice on communicating expectations and access concerns. Advisory only.

units.why: "There is no single approach to AI that will work for every course, discipline, or assignment" leaves the rule to each course, so P04 and informs.
units.anchor: no single approach to AI that will work for every course, discipline, or assignment

units.why: "students may benefit from using AI to brainstorm, practice, revise, or evaluate information" is a factual statement of where AI helps; P15 would cover brainstorming only and P02 is a default rule, so P04 (context-dependent) fits as the framing; informs.
units.anchor: students may benefit from using AI to brainstorm, practice, revise, or evaluate information

units.why: "the use of AI may interfere with the development of foundational knowledge or essential disciplinary skills" gives the reason for limiting AI in foundation-building work, so P42 and informs.
units.anchor: the use of AI may interfere with the development of foundational knowledge
units.frag_start: In others, the use of AI

units.why: "The goal is not to adopt AI simply because it is available or to avoid it entirely" states the guidance principle for the page, so P56 (framework principle) and informs.
units.anchor: not to adopt AI simply because it is available or to avoid it entirely

units.why: "Before deciding whether students should use AI, begin with what you want them to learn" tells instructors how to set the course rule, so P04 (instructor decides), should, before-course.
units.anchor: Before deciding whether students should use AI, begin with what you want them to learn

units.why: "a student might appropriately use AI to generate possible topics for a project but still need to develop the final research question independently" permits AI for ideas while students decide; P32 (student stays thinker) fits over P15 because of the "independently" limit.
units.anchor: use AI to generate possible topics for a project but still need to develop

units.why: "The role of AI should be determined by the purpose of the learning experience, not simply by the tool's capabilities" says the rule is set per learning experience, so P04, should.
units.anchor: The role of AI should be determined by the purpose of the learning experience

units.why: "Your approach to AI may vary across courses—and even across assignments within the same course" is per-assignment variation, so P04 and informs.
units.anchor: Your approach to AI may vary across courses

units.why: "The following three approaches can provide a useful starting point" introduces limited, guided and integrated categories of AI use, so P05 (named tiers) and informs.
units.anchor: The following three approaches can provide a useful starting point

units.why: "The use of AI may be restricted when students need to develop or demonstrate essential skills independently" defines the "limited" tier; P05 since it names a level, may, restrict.
units.anchor: The use of AI may be restricted when students need to develop or demonstrate

units.why: Under the limited tier: "Completing exams, quizzes, or other assessments of independent learning" is listed as a case where AI may be restricted, so P22 (no AI on exams) with may since the document only suggests it.
units.anchor: Completing exams, quizzes, or other assessments of independent learning

units.why: "Developing skills they will need before using AI responsibly in more advanced work" names a staged logic (skills first, AI later), so P08 and may.
units.anchor: Developing skills they will need before using AI responsibly in more advanced work

units.why: "Students still benefit from understanding why its use is restricted and how completing the work independently supports their learning" is the skill-building rationale, P41; informs.
units.anchor: completing the work independently supports their learning

units.why: The guided tier: "faculty clearly identify which uses are permitted, which are not" sets per-part permissions, so P05 and should.
units.anchor: faculty clearly identify which uses are permitted, which are not

units.why: The same guided-tier sentence says faculty identify "how students should document their use of AI", a disclosure expectation, so P24 and should; the permitted/not part is coded under P05.
units.anchor: how students should document their use of AI

units.why: Guided example "Brainstorm possible topics" is an AI use students may be permitted; P15.
units.anchor: Brainstorm possible topics

units.why: "Generate practice questions" is listed as a permitted guided use; P14 (practice and study aids).
units.anchor: Generate practice questions

units.why: "Create an initial outline" is a permitted guided use, writing support; P18 (prose) over P15 since the outline is a writing step.
units.anchor: Create an initial outline

units.why: "Receive suggestions for revising grammar or organization" is a writing-support use that may be permitted, P18.
units.anchor: Receive suggestions for revising grammar or organization

units.why: "Explore alternative explanations of a difficult concept" is AI as a tutor for concepts, P12.
units.anchor: Explore alternative explanations of a difficult concept

units.why: "AI may be intentionally incorporated when evaluating, using, or understanding AI is part of the learning goal" defines the integrated tier, so P05; unit leans toward encouraging use.
units.anchor: AI may be intentionally incorporated when evaluating, using, or understanding AI

units.why: "AI is not completing students' learning. It becomes material for analysis, decision-making, and reflection" limits integrated use so AI does not do the learning; P32.
units.anchor: AI is not completing students' learning
units.frag_start: In this approach, AI is not

units.why: "Critique an AI-generated response" is an example integrated assignment that is built around AI, so P35 (redesign assignments).
units.anchor: Critique an AI-generated response

units.why: "Identify inaccuracies, bias, or missing perspectives" asks students to critically evaluate AI output; P31.
units.anchor: Identify inaccuracies, bias, or missing perspectives

units.why: "Explain which parts of the output they accepted, changed, or rejected" is a reflection on AI use, so P26.
units.anchor: Explain which parts of the output they accepted, changed, or rejected

units.why: Question 1: "Identify the knowledge and skills that students must practice without AI assistance" tells instructors to decide which skills stay AI-free; P04 (instructor decides), should.
units.anchor: Identify the knowledge and skills that students must practice without AI assistance

units.why: "AI use should extend or support the learning process rather than replace it" keeps students as the primary thinkers, P32, should.
units.anchor: AI use should extend or support the learning process rather than replace it

units.why: "AI may be less appropriate when the purpose of an assignment is for students to develop an idea, make a decision, solve a problem, or practice a skill" explains when AI undercuts learning, P41.
units.anchor: AI may be less appropriate when the purpose of an assignment is for students

units.why: "If AI can complete the most important thinking required by the assignment, the expectations or design may need to be reconsidered" tells instructors to redesign assignments, P35.
units.anchor: the expectations or design may need to be reconsidered

units.why: "Students may encounter very different expectations across their courses" notes that rules differ by course, P11, informs.
units.anchor: Students may encounter very different expectations across their courses

units.why: "Clearly communicate whether AI is permitted, limited, required, or prohibited for each major assignment" asks for an assignment-level AI statement, P09.
units.anchor: Clearly communicate whether AI is permitted, limited, required, or prohibited

units.why: "Consider whether students will need to create an account, pay for access, enter personal information" raises access and privacy issues for instructors choosing tools; P51 (equity and cost), should.
units.anchor: Consider whether students will need to create an account, pay for

units.why: "When AI use is required, provide an appropriate alternative for students who cannot use the selected tool or prefer not to" is an alternatives rule, P51, should.
units.anchor: provide an appropriate alternative for students who cannot use the selected tool

units.why: "A syllabus statement can explain your overall approach to AI" with the listed contents is guidance that the syllabus carry an AI statement, P09, may.
units.anchor: A syllabus statement can explain your overall approach to AI

units.why: The list item "Whether AI is generally permitted, limited, or prohibited" tells instructors to state the default in the syllabus; P09.
units.anchor: Whether AI is generally permitted, limited, or prohibited

units.why: "Student responsibilities for accuracy and source verification" is a syllabus item on checking AI output, P31.
units.anchor: Student responsibilities for accuracy and source verification

units.why: "Expectations for acknowledging AI use" is a syllabus item on disclosure, P24.
units.anchor: Expectations for acknowledging AI use

units.why: "How students should ask questions when expectations are unclear" is a syllabus item on asking when unsure, P10.
units.anchor: How students should ask questions when expectations are unclear

units.why: "Faculty should adapt these examples to match their course outcomes" says sample statements are adapted per course; P04, should.
units.anchor: Faculty should adapt these examples to match their course outcomes

units.why: "Whatever language you choose, discuss it with students rather than relying on the written statement alone" asks for explicit communication beyond the syllabus, P09 course-start.
units.anchor: discuss it with students rather than relying on the written statement alone

units.why: "Consider discussing AI expectations early in the semester and again when introducing major assignments" is a communication timing rule, P09.
units.anchor: Consider discussing AI expectations early in the semester and again when introducing

units.why: "How to ask for clarification before using a tool" is a topic instructors should discuss; students ask before using AI, P10.
units.anchor: How to ask for clarification before using a tool

units.why: "Faculty expertise remains essential for evaluating accuracy, appropriateness, and alignment with learning goals" is a statement about the role of faculty; no type covers it (P46 is on grades), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Faculty expertise remains essential for evaluating accuracy, appropriateness, and alignment
units.uncovered_note: Faculty expertise remains essential to evaluate AI accuracy and fit with learning goals, regardless of AI approach.

units.why: "Students should not enter private, protected, or personally identifiable information into public AI tools" is a privacy rule for students, P50, should-not.
units.anchor: Students should not enter private, protected, or personally identifiable information into public AI tools

units.why: "AI-generated information may be inaccurate, biased, incomplete, or supported by fabricated sources" warns that output is unreliable, P31.
units.anchor: AI-generated information may be inaccurate, biased, incomplete, or supported by fabricated sources

units.why: "Students remain responsible for the work they submit" is accountability for submitted work, P29, must.
units.anchor: Students remain responsible for the work they submit

units.why: "Expectations should be communicated at both the course and assignment levels" is a two-level communication rule, P09.
units.anchor: Expectations should be communicated at both the course and assignment levels

units.why: The consultation offer lists "Developing course or assignment-level AI expectations" and other help, which is support for faculty, P63.
units.anchor: Developing course or assignment-level AI expectations
units.frag_start: CMU faculty can receive support with

documents.unit: Office of Curriculum and Instructional Support
documents.title: Sample Statements for Teaching Syllabi
documents.stance_why: These are optional templates for instructors ("Faculty should adapt these examples"); the statements ban only submitting AI output as your own work and say other uses are for the instructor to decide, so the document delegates.
documents.summary: Library of sample syllabus statements; the AI parts are an academic-integrity statement and an optional AI-generated-materials statement that treat submitting AI output as one's own as prohibited. Instructors adopt or adapt them.

units.why: "This modified statement includes suggested language regarding AI-related content" offers an optional syllabus statement for instructors to include, P09, may.
units.anchor: This modified statement includes suggested language regarding AI-related content.

units.why: "Written or other work students submit must be the product of their own efforts" requires submitted work be students' own, P29, must.
units.anchor: Written or other work students submit must be the product of their own efforts

units.why: "submitting artificial intelligence (AI)-generated products as your own original work, is prohibited" bans passing off AI output as one's own, P19, must-not.
units.anchor: submitting artificial intelligence (AI)-generated products as your own original work, is prohibited

units.why: The same sentence puts AI-generated work in "Academic dishonesty, which includes cheating, plagiarism", i.e. misconduct under integrity rules, so P36; the ban itself is coded under P19.
units.anchor: Academic dishonesty, which includes cheating, plagiarism, and other forms of dishonest

units.why: "Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Google AI, Boost.ai, Jasper, etc.)" defines which tools the statement covers, P61.
units.anchor: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Google AI, Boost.ai, Jasper, etc.)

units.why: "Submitting text and other products generated by AI tools and platforms as your own original work is prohibited" bans submitting AI output as one's own, P19, must-not.
units.anchor: AI tools and platforms as your own original work is prohibited

units.why: "a violation of CMU’s Academic Integrity policy" treats unauthorized AI submission as an integrity violation, P36.
units.anchor: a violation of CMU’s Academic Integrity policy

units.why: "If the use of AI tools and platforms is appropriate within the context of a course" leaves the allowance to the course, P04, informs.
units.anchor: If the use of AI tools and platforms is appropriate within the context
units.frag_start: If the use of AI tools

units.why: "appropriate methods of citation for direct quotations, ideas, diagrams, code, or paraphrased text generated through AI will be provided by your instructor" says the instructor gives citation methods, P24 (not P25: no detail required).
units.anchor: appropriate methods of citation for direct quotations, ideas, diagrams, code, or paraphrased text
units.frag_start: If the use of AI tools

notes: Coder B. Only the three included university-layer documents were coded; no school, computing or course documents were collected. The sample-statements page was long; only its two AI-related statements were coded.
